nodes.label: Confidence Scoring Rubric
nodes.rationale: Discrete buckets (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) replace a continuous 0-1 range because production data showed models collapsing continuous guidance to a binary (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+); models follow discrete rubrics more faithfully than free-floating ranges.

nodes.label: Node ID Format Rule
nodes.rationale: IDs must be {full-repo-relative-stem}_{entity}, every path segment kept (not just the immediate parent), deterministic from the label alone, never chunk-suffixed — must match what the AST extractor generates or same-named symbols in different directories create orphan ghost-duplicate nodes.

nodes.label: No API Key Required Rule
nodes.rationale: Code is AST-extracted with no LLM/key at all; semantic extraction (docs/papers/images) uses Gemini only if GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY is already set, otherwise the host agent itself is the LLM via dispatched subagents. graphify never reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY, so the agent must never block on or prompt for a missing key.

nodes.label: graph.json Shrink Guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json() returns False (writes nothing) if the newly built graph has fewer nodes than the existing graphify-out/graph.json, so a failed/partial extraction can never silently clobber a good prior graph; GRAPH_REPORT.md and the analysis sidecar are only (re)written when the write actually happened.

nodes.label: Read version.py for Release Version
nodes.rationale: version.py stays the single, human-controlled source of truth: bump it (alongside moving CHANGELOG [Unreleased] to the new version) and this workflow only creates the tag/release from it — it never commits back to main, so there is no risk of a push loop.

nodes.label: CI Workflow (ruff + pytest)
nodes.rationale: This is the quality gate that runs on every push to main and every PR; the separate release workflow only tags/publishes when version.py is bumped, keeping linting/testing and releasing as two independent concerns.

nodes.label: Backlog Item: restore_task/restore_column FK Crash on Ctrl+Z
nodes.rationale: restore_task/restore_column fall back to the snapshot's own stored parent id (column_id/board_id) with no guard that it still exists, while tasks.column_id/columns.board_id are NOT NULL FKs with ON DELETE CASCADE — reachable via delete task, delete its column, Ctrl+Z twice (or one level up with column/board). Fixed with a new database/columns.py::get_column (symmetric with get_board) plus an existence guard in each restore_* function, returning None instead of crashing.

nodes.label: Tech Debt: restore_column/restore_board Not Atomic Across Children
nodes.rationale: Each nested restore_task/restore_column call opens its own connection/transaction, so a failure partway through undoing a multi-task column/board leaves a partially-restored result instead of all-or-nothing; low practical impact (needs a mid-restore failure like disk-full), deliberately not acted on.
nodes.norm_label: tech debt: restore_column/restore_board not atomic across children

nodes.label: Constrained Query Vocabulary Expansion
nodes.rationale: graphify query matches nodes via case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming/synonyms/cross-language matching, so a wording mismatch between the user's question and the graph's own labels collapses results to noise; fixed by expanding the query against the graph's real label vocabulary first, picking only tokens that already exist in it (never inventing tokens).

nodes.label: build_merge Replace-on-Re-extract (#1344)
nodes.rationale: Every source_file present in the new extraction chunks is dropped from the base graph before merging, so re-extracted/changed files never accumulate as duplicates; prune_sources is therefore reserved only for genuinely deleted files, not changed ones.

nodes.label: Semantic Manifest Stamping Gate (#2015/#1948)
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files (docs/papers/images) that ACTUALLY produced output this run are stamped in the manifest; a changed file whose chunk failed or was omitted must stay unstamped so the next --update re-queues it — otherwise it is marked done and its content is lost forever.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS if unsure), never skip the corpus size warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion scores, never run HTML viz on >5000 nodes without warning — keeps the audit trail honest rather than optimistic.
